movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
Metagross's great typing, stats, and movepool allow it to function as a solid bulky attacker, handling threats like Latios and Ogerpon-C. Heavy Slam is a reliable STAB move, taking advantage of Metagross's large weight to do solid damage to threats like Hydrapple, Mandibuzz, and Greninja. Stealth Rock also allows Metagross to function as an entry hazard setter, while Bullet Punch gives Metagross a STAB priority move to circumvent its below average Speed, hitting foes like Ogerpon-C and Mamoswine. Knock Off can be used to cripple checks like Slowking and Hydrapple by removing their items, while Earthquake can be used to hit Steel-types such as Excadrill, Heatran, and Cobalion. Leftovers is crucial for maintaining Metagross's longevity, since it doesn't get a recovery move. 96 Speed EVs allow Metagross to outspeed maximum Speed Adamant Azumarill. Tera Dark allows Metagross to turn its weaknesses to Dark and Ghost into resistances while also boosting the power of its Knock Off, while Tera Water allows it to resist Fire-type attacks from Hisuian Arcanine and Skeledirge and tank Belly Drum Azumarill's boosted Aqua Jet.

Metagross does best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its good mix of power and bulk. Teammates like Tornadus-T, Mandibuzz, and Hydrapple all provide a Ground resistance that covers Metagross's weakness. In return, Metagross answers Ogerpon-C, which is scary for the former two and takes pressure off of Hydrapple. However, it is important to note that Tornadus-T cannot switch into Rhyperior safely, so answers to it like Slowking or the aforementioned Hydrapple are appreciated. Metagross is also weak to Fire-type moves from Pokemon like Hisuian Arcanine and Skeledirge, so Water types like Rotom-W and Slowking can help tank these attacks, both of which can use pivot moves to bring Metagross in safely. In general, Metagross benefits greatly from pivots that can bring it in safely, so U-turn users like Lokix, Ogerpon, and Scizor also make great teammates. Metagross tends to struggle with bulky Flying-types like Skarmory and Mandibuzz, so it benefits from teammates that can handle these two, such as Rhyperior and Sandy Shocks. These two Pokemon also act as alternate Stealth Rock users, which not only synergizes well with Metagross's Knock Off but also allows it to run Bullet Punch. The latter can also act as a spiker to form a hazard-stacking core with Metagross.

movesets.name: Suicide Lead
movesets.description:
Explosion Metagross is an offensive Pokemon with some defensive utility and a simple gameplan: set Stealth Rock then use Explosion. Explosion does a lot of damage to the tier's defensive Pokemon like Hydrapple and Slowking. Earthquake lets it hit the Steel-types that resist its Explosion and Heavy Slam, like Heatran and Excadrill. Stealth Rock gives it excellent utility, setting entry hazards while the foe switches out. Bullet Punch is useful when running an alternative hazard setter, as it can clean up foes at low HP. Metagross can utilize its fantastic typing to defensively check Pokemon like Latios and Hydrapple. Custap Berry alleviates how low Metagross may get in the process by gaining priority on Explosion. Normal Gem can allow it to KO some important targets, such as maximum Defense Hydrapple after Tera Normal. The given Speed investment allows Metagross to outspeed Mandibuzz and Azumarill but 196 Speed EVs can allow it to outspeed targets like Tinkaton and Choice Band Tyranitar; however, doing so would sacrifice some of the bulk that lets it check Ogerpon-C and Latios. Tera Normal lets Metagross power up its Explosion, letting it potentially OHKO Slowking and Hydrapple with chip, but beware that most of its defensive utility comes from its typing, so only use Tera if Metagross needs Tera Normal to KO the foe.

Metagross fits best on offensive structures, as it lures in Skarmory and Hydrapple and weakens them for the rest of the team to exploit. Excadrill is an amazing partner, especially considering how much it threatens Skeledirge and Rotom-W, Pokemon that Metagross hates. Thundurus and Sandy Shocks also are good partners, as they enjoy Metagross's ability to switch into Latios and weaken Hydrapple. Sandy Shocks can also act as an alternate Stealth Rock setter. Metagross also enjoys Sticky Web support from Araquanid, allowing it to outspeed Pokemon like Tyranitar and Tinkaton while keeping its bulk as well as offensive checks like non-Heavy-Duty Boots Mamoswine. Ghost-type Pokemon like Sinistcha and Pecharunt can cause problems, as they block Metagross's Explosion attempts while threatening it with Shadow Ball, so it appreciates offensive Dark-types like Tyranitar and Lokix.

movesets.name: Stealth Rock (Psychic)
movesets.description:
By virtue of its great bulk and defensive typing, Metagross makes for great entry hazard support for Psychic teams, dealing well with common hazard controllers like Hatterene and Tentacruel. Psychic Fangs threatens the aforementioned Tentacruel as well as other Poison- and Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Okidogi; it also eases the Fairy and Ice matchups due to breaking dual screens. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Brambleghast, and Indeedee while also removing items from foes that are reliant on them like Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Leftovers from Corviknight. Bullet Punch can be run over Psychic Fangs or Knock Off to revenge kill faster threats such as Iron Valiant, Flutter Mane, and Weavile. However, most of Metagross's teammates provide great speed control, and running a second Steel-type STAB move on Metagross restricts its number of potential targets. Heavy Slam threatens Fairy- and Ice-types such as Hatterene, Alolan Ninetales, and Articuno. 96 Speed EVs allow Metagross to outspeed Adamant Azumarill.

Wallbreakers such as Choice Band Hoopa-U and Choice Specs Latios appreciate Metagross setting entry hazards to help them wallbreak. Hoopa-U also takes on Dark-, Ghost-, and Steel-types such as specially defensive Ting-Lu, Gholdengo, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra, while Latios provides a Ground immunity and handles Steel- and Ground-types like Archaludon, Corviknight, Gliscor, and Great Tusk. Deoxys-S forms a hazard-stacking core with Metagross thanks to Spikes, appreciating it running Stealth Rock so it can run another utility option such as Taunt. Hatterene is a potential wincon for Psychic teams that appreciates entry hazards wearing down incoming foes such as Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Scarf Enamorus, and it is a useful asset in the Dark and Dragon matchups to deal with threats such as Sableye, Hydreigon, Garchomp, and Raging Bolt. Additionally, Hatterene provides hazard control thanks to Magic Bounce. Choice Scarf Latias appreciates Metagross taking out Fairy-types like Hatterene and Iron Valiant, and in return, it provides a Ground immunity to switch into and deal with Great Tusk and Landorus, as well as Choice-locking walls like Ting-Lu and Corviknight by giving them its Choice Scarf with Trick. Lastly, late-game sweepers such as Agility Iron Crown, Agility Gallade, and Choice Scarf Iron Boulder appreciate Metagross setting entry hazards, weakening walls with Knock Off, and revenge killing boosted sweepers with Bullet Punch to start a sweep of their own. Additionally, Iron Boulder threatens the likes of Ogerpon-H, Hisuian Arcanine, Volcarona, and Meowscarada.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Psychic)
movesets.description:
With a Choice Band, Metagross becomes a devastating wallbreaker for Psychic teams thanks to its incredible Attack stat, immunity to Intimidate, and incredible priority move. Heavy Slam makes full use of Metagross's immense weight to deal with threats like Azumarill. Alternatively, Meteor Mash allows Metagross to OKHO heavier targets like Kyurem and Tyranitar along with getting a possible Attack boost at the cost of some accuracy. Bullet Punch provides a solid form of priority to deal with faster targets such as Flutter Mane, Alolan Ninetales, Weavile, and weakened Hoopa-U. Knock Off allows Metagross to force progress against targets that can otherwise handle it like Skarmory and Corviknight by removing crucial held items; it also threatens Ghost-types such as Air Balloon Gholdengo and Sinistcha. Finally, Earthquake hits Steel- and Electric-type threats like Hisuian Goodra, Magnezone, and Raging Bolt. The EV Spread used allows Metagross to outspeed Adamant Azumarill while surviving hits such as Modest +1 Raging Bolt's Thunderbolt.

Choice Specs Latios, when paired with Metagross, forms a devastating wallbreaker core; Latios cleanly removes physical walls such as Skarmory, Corviknight, and Hippowdon, while Metagross can remove threats Latios struggles against such as Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, and Flutter Mane. Deoxys-S provides solid entry hazard stacking capabilities, further increasing Metagross's wallbreaking capabilities. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder provides a solid form of speed control along with dealing with Fire-type threats such as Iron Moth, Volcarona, and Ogerpon-H. Assault Vest Hoopa-U can deal with problematic Ghost-types that handle Metagross like Gholdengo and Hisuian Zoroark with ease. Slowbro supports Metagross by dealing with Fire- and Ground-types like Cinderace, Great Tusk, and Mamoswine along with providing Thunder Wave support, allowing Metagross to outspeed threats such as Heatran and Cinderace. Choice Scarf Latias can support Metagross by dealing with threats such as non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and provides Healing Wish support to heal Metagross. Hatterene provides utility in Magic Bounce to prevent entry hazards along with dealing with Dark-type threats such as Sableye, Mandibuzz, and Roaring Moon, which otherwise threaten Metagross. Armarouge deals with Steel-type threats such as Scizor, Archaludon, and Skarmory that handle Metagross.

movesets.name: Bulky Offense
movesets.description:
• Good bulk, priority, and Clear Body stopping common Attack debuffers like Flutter Mane and Dragonite from easily setting up gives Metagross a niche over Scizor, despite the irritating weakness to Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • Psychic Fangs: Despite the iffy coverage, Psychic Fangs is a great STAB attack for having a high chance of OHKOing offensive Urshifu-R and nullifying Aurora Veil from the troublesome Alolan Ninetales.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake provides fantastic coverage against most Steel-types like Gholdengo and Archaludon, although it misses out on Corviknight and Tera Steel Latias.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch chills Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Garchomp to the bone, all of which are common Metagross checks otherwise.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off gives Metagross some useful utility, particularly against Porygon2's Eviolite and Assault Vest holders that may switch in like Ursaluna-B. It's also good coverage against Gholdengo.

  • EV Spread: This spread survives Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake and Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

Other Options

  • Alternate Steel-type STAB Moves: Hard Press can be used to OHKO Flutter Mane, but the poor coverage can make it difficult to justify. Meteor Mash doesn't even have to worry about the target being at full HP, and the Attack boost can be dangerous, but the accuracy is an issue.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot smacks Ursaluna-B and Dondozo for far more damage than Metagross's physical attacks do, although it's a difficult move to fit in.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite Metagross's typing being decent in a vacuum, the Ghost and Dark weaknesses are a big enough problem to often justify Terastallization.

  • Water: Tera Water stops Tera Water Urshifu-R from breaking through Metagross, and it even helps against Choice Specs Chi-Yu if it's locked into a Fire-type attack. It also cushions Metagross from Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel, although Horn Leech will now easily 2HKO.

  • Ground: Tera Ground gets rid of Metagross's troublesome Dark, Ghost, and Ground weaknesses and powers up Earthquake enough to put offensive Archaludon into the KO range of Bullet Punch. Thanks to Metagross's original typing, it can also shock Raging Bolt's attempts to revenge kill.

  • Steel: Buffing up Bullet Punch is helpful for cleaning up weakened teams, with most offensive Flutter Mane in particular now being OHKOed by it. While it doesn't OHKO Chien-Pao, removing the Dark weakness means any that lack an offensive item will fail to 2HKO Tera Steel Metagross with Sucker Punch.

  • Dark: Tera Dark works nicely with Knock Off, OHKOing offensive Gholdengo and giving Metagross important resistances to Ghost and Dark.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest is Metagross's best tool for tanking hits, ensuring foes like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolt won't easily cleave through it.

  • Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy is a high-risk, high-reward approach to Metagross, taking advantage of its great physical bulk to turn the tables on common physical attackers and sweep late-game with Bullet Punch, like against Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch and Landorus-T's Earthquake.

strategies.overview:
• Metagross serves as a good defensive Pokemon on balance teams thanks to its great defenses that are bolstered even further by Assault Vest, its good ability, and its nice defensive typing against foes like Raging Bolt and Iron Crown. Its access to coverage and high Attack stat make it appreciated as an offensive threat too.

  • Metagross can pair well with offensive Pokemon like Flutter Mane and Landorus, which can help deal with the Dark-, Ghost-, and Fire-types that threaten it like Urshifu-S, Gholdengo, and Entei. Another excellent partner can be Ogerpon-W, which has great synergy with Metagross, being able to deal with Ground-types like Landorus and redirect Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao, while Metagross can help Ogerpon-W against Rillaboom and Raging Bolt.

  • Before Terastallizing, Metagross can be overwhelmed by Pokemon like Kingambit, Chi-Yu, and Entei, making defensive partners like Amoonguss and Incineroar appreciated. Rillaboom can also be a good teammate for Metagross, providing it with passive recovery and utility via Grassy Terrain and Fake Out, respectively.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Stomping Tantrum lets Metagross hit Fire- and Steel-types likeIncineroar, Entei, and Kingambit and can also help against targets like Raging Bolt. Stomping Tantrum in particular is important to hit Steel-types like Iron Crown, as they wall Metagross's STAB moves.

  • Bullet Punch can be used to help pick off weakened foes like Flutter Mane.

  • With an Assault Vest, Metagross can almost always survive Earth Power from Landorus

  • With the given EV spread, Metagross almost always survives Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao when using Tera Dragon, and it is only 3HKOed by -1 Adamant Chien-Pao's Sacred Sword when using Tera Steel. The Speed EVs let it outspeed -1 Adamant Landorus-T, as well as Roaring Moon and Adamant Chien-Pao when in Tailwind.

  • Tera Dragon lets Metagross handle Fire-types like Chi-Yu and Entei in a pinch, and it can also be useful to deal with Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Tera Steel helps remove its weakness against Pokemon like Kingambit, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao, and it can also give Bullet Punch a chance to OHKO offensive Flutter Mane.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 4 onwards

Price Range: 12-13 points

Overview: Metagross is a valuable pick thanks to its strong wallbreaking ability, coveted Steel typing, great stat distribution, and versatility. Few Pokemon can reliably check Metagross when powered up by a damage-boosting item or with the ability to Tera due to its wide movepool of strong physical attacks. Metagross also has the ability to take on a more supportive role as a bulky Steel-type with access to Stealth Rock and Knock Off. While Metagross has many strengths, it is held back by its incredibly awkward Speed and a decent amount of common weaknesses, causing Metagross to fall to the middle of most drafts.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Metagross can utilize its strong Attack stat and powerful STAB and coverage attacks to severely weaken teams. These sets will commonly use a damage-boosting item such as Choice Band to give Metagross incredibly threatening immediate power as it lacks setup.

Offensive Utility: Metagross can use its number of supportive options paired with its existing offensive prowess to play a hybrid role of utility and offense. On these sets, Metagross can run Stealth Rock, Knock Off, and even dual screens to support your team while still maintaining an offensive presence.

Agility Sweeper: Metagross is able to become a capable sweeper through the use of Agility to overcome its awkward Speed. Metagross can simply use its naturally high Attack stat, or it can use an item to gain power, such as Weakness Policy, leveraging its natural bulk, or Power Herb in combination with Meteor Beam, enabling it to be a special sweeper.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Heavy Slam, Meteor Mash, Iron Head, Psychic Fangs, Bullet Punch

Setup Moves: Agility, Hone Claws, Iron Defense, Trailblaze

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Knock Off, Light Screen, Reflect, Trick, Brick Break, Psychic Noise, Rock Tomb

Coverage: Earthquake, Ice Punch, Thunder Punch, Stone Edge, Rock Slide, Body Press, Hammer Arm, Grass Knot, Shadow Claw

Niche Moves

Explosion: Explosion can be used as a very powerful one time attack to severely damage or eliminate a wall while providing momentum to your team.

Endure: Endure can be found on sets with a Custap Berry or Weakness Policy, allowing Metagross to survive an attack and allow your item to activate.

Meteor Beam: With a respectable Special Attack stat, Metagross can utilize Meteor Beam paired with a Power Herb to boost its Special Attack and allow it to run special sets in matchups where that may see success. These sets will commonly be paired with Agility to increase Speed, special STAB options such as Flash Cannon and Psychic, and coverage attacks like Grass Knot.

Gravity: Metagross can use Gravity to boost the accuracy of some attacks and temporarily remove Ground immunities. Metagross may also set this field condition if teammates benefit from this support.

Common Items

Choice Band: Choice Band allows a wallbreaking Metagross to tear down walls, often enabling it to even break through foes that resist its attacks. This also helps Metagross to clean up late-game with its priority Bullet Punch.

Leftovers / Sitrus Berry: Leftovers can provide extra longevity for bulkier sets that aim to serve as a check to specific foes.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Against entry hazard stacking teams, Heavy-Duty Boots, can prevent Spike stacking from weakening Metagross.

Resistance Berries: Resistance Berries such as Colbur Berry and Shuca Berry can provide Metagross an extra turn to absorb an expected super effective attack and set up Stealth Rock or attack back.

Weakness Policy: Metagross may use its number of common weaknesses and natural bulk in its favor to gain a lot of power. Weakness Policy is typically found on sets with Agility to attempt to sweep games or clean up a weakened team.

Niche Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf lets Metagross overcome its mediocre Speed stat and catch foes by surprise with fast, powerful attacks. You will often use Trick on Choice Scarf sets to impede the effectiveness of an incoming wall and give the ability to switch moves.

Damage-boosting Items: Damage-boosting items such as Expert Belt and Metal Coat can help wallbreaking sets increase their damage and provide more flexibility by allowing Metagross to switch attacks.

Assault Vest: When additional bulk is needed, Metagross can use an Assault Vest while still taking advantage of its movepool of strong STAB, coverage priority, and utility attacks.

Custap Berry: Custap Berry allows a weakened Metagross to gain an additional turn despite its Speed stat. This can pair well with Endure to ensure the activation of this item.

Tera

While not the most common Tera Captain due to its mediocre Speed and premier higher-tier options available, Metagross can be a strong Tera Captain. Metagross can use the STAB-enhancing Tera Steel to annihilate almost any foe and strengthen its Bullet Punch. Metagross will also use some defensive Tera types such as Fairy, Water, and Poison to increase longevity and improve matchups. It can become a far better sweeping threat with Agility on Tera variants, and picking up a strong typing can pair well with its fantastic defenses.

Draft Strategy

As a middle-round pick that will not always be your Tera Captain, Metagross should not be the star of your draft. That being said, the versatility Metagross provides through its wallbreaking, bulk, utility, and late-game cleaning potential will be greatly supportive to many team structures.

Sweepers and Wallbreakers: While it's a fantastic wallbreaker itself, Metagross can be excellent when paired with Pokemon that can weaken foes enough for it to clean up late-game with its Bullet Priority. Pokemon such as Garchomp, Iron Moth, and Ogerpon-W can fill this role.

Entry Hazard Setters: Metagross fits well on teams with hazard setters, letting another teammate set hazards provides Metagross an additional moveslot and item flexibility. It also can become incredibly difficult to avoid using a Choice Band or other damage-boosting items with Metagross, which can claim KOs after hazard chip damage. There is further synergy with these team structures, as Metagross can consistently remove items with Knock Off. Hisuian Samurrott, Gliscor, and Glimmora all pair well with Metagross in this role.

Speed Control: One of Metagross's main weaknesses is a very subpar Speed stat for an offensive Pokemon. As a result, Metagross enjoys fast teammates such as Tornadus-T, Darkrai, and Meowscarada.

Reliable Pivots: To maximize Metagrosses's wallbreaking potential, teammates that can allow Metagross safely enter to the field are fantastic teammates. Reliable pivots such as Zapdos, Landorus-T, and Rotom-W can provide safe entry for Metagross numerous times over the course of a match, providing it many opportunities to tear down walls.

Checks and Counters

Physically Bulky Walls: While it's a very potent wallbreaker, Metagross can be checked by a number of common walls if they have a strong type advantage or enough natural bulk. Pokemon such as Deoxys-D, Ting-Lu, and Alomomola can all effectively serve as Metagross checks.

Faster Offensive Foes: Metagross can be hindered a great deal by its Speed stat and common weaknesses, allowing it to be offensively checked by Pokemon not threatened by its priority move. Pokemon such as Urshifu-S, Iron Moth, and Garchomp outspeed and threaten Metagross off the field.

Burn Infliction: As a result of its mediocre Speed, many Pokemon can outspeed Metagross and burn it, or live an attack due to their bulk and typing and inflict status. Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Skeledirge can diminish the efficacy of Metagross by burning it.

Knock Off: Knock Off is very threatening to Metagross, as it is weak to the move and often requires an item to hit damage thresholds or have longevity.

movesets.name: Weakness Policy
movesets.description:
• Heavy Slam is for Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Whimsicott as well as light Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Porygon-Z.
  • Meteor Mash can be used for consistent damage, being particularly useful against heavy Rock- and Ice-type Pokemon
  • Bullet Punch is useful for securing KOs on faster Pokemon, Encore + Disable Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales, and pinch Berry users such as Sneasler.
  • Earthquake is for Hisuian Goodra and Metagross mirror matchups.
  • Psychic Fangs is for Pecharunt and some Urshifu-R sets. It also helps break Reflect from Pokemon like Primarina and Kyurem.
  • Hone Claws allows Metagross to set up against Counter users like Hisuian Goodra, which cannot be OHKOed by Metagross's Earthquake, allowing it to OHKO Hisuian Goodra with +1 Earthquake.
  • The bulk EVs let Metagross survive Modest Choice Specs Kyurem's Earth Power and Adamant Choice Band Haxorus's Earthquake. The rest of the EVs are put into Attack.
  • If Metagross is not running Hone Claws to set up Attack against Counter Hisuian Goodra, it can chip away at Hisuian Goodra's HP with Bullet Punch, since Counter won't do much, then it can KO Hisuian Goodra when it's in Earthquake's KO range.
  • Since Metagross is weak to Fire-, Dark-, and Ground-type moves, a Water- or Fairy-type Pokemon like Manaphy or Primarina makes a good teammate.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
• Heavy Slam is for Primarina, Iron Valiant, and Sylveon.
  • Bullet Punch lets Metagross deal with Encore + Disable Iron Valiant and KO Haxorus and Custap or Sitrus Berry Primarina after Heavy Slam.
  • Earthquake beats Iron Crown and is the best option Raging Bolt.
  • Psychic Fangs gives Metagross a better matchup against Pecharunt and Reflect Primarina, while Ice Punch gives Metagross the best odds against Assault Vest Landorus-T, and Life Orb Landorus.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Metagross to survive Knock Off from Jolly Choice Band Meowscarada. The Special Defense EVs allow Metagross to take 2 Thunderbolts from Booster Energy Raging Bolt. The remaining EVs are put into Attack to maximize odds against Choice Band Earthquake Haxorus.

movesets.name: Air Balloon
movesets.description:
• Air Balloon + Iron Defense + Body Press allows Metagross to lure in physical Ground-types like Ursaluna and Donphan to gain a surprise win.
  • Heavy Slam + Bullet Punch allows Metagross to maintain good matchups against all common Fairy-types. Having two Steel-type moves secures the matchup against Fairy-type Encore + Disable users like Iron Valiant, Alolan Ninetales, and the rare Gardevoir. Meteor Mash lets Metagross defeat Kyurem at the cost of losing to Primarina and lower accuracy.
  • This EV spread allows Metagross to always survive a Knock Off from Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada or a Focus Blast from Timid Choice Specs Valiant. The Speed EVs enable Metagross to always outspeed base 50 speed Pokemon without a Speed-boosting nature, such as Ursaluna, Iron Hands, and Donphan.
  • Do not use Iron Defense against strong Dark-types like Meowscarada and Chien-Pao. Body Press followed by Bullet Punch KOes Meowscarada and Chien-Pao, although Chien-Pao's Throat Chop can sometimes OHKO Metagross.
  • Against Ursaluna, use Iron Defense twice, and then OHKO it with Body Press to play around Counter.
  • To make an effective team with Metagross, be sure you are covering Fire-types like Volcanion and Volcarona, Ghost-types like Spectrier, Dragapult, and Pecharunt, strong Dark-types like Urshifu-S, Galarian Moltres, and Hoopa-U, and miscellaneous strong special attackers like Raging Bolt and Zapdos. Some examples of partners that could cover some of these weaknesses include Ursaluna, Walking Wake, and Galarian Moltres.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Heavy Slam is used to defeat non-Custap Berry Primarina, while Meteor Mash allows Metagross to beat Kyurem. Both moves do well into Sylveon, Porygon-Z, and Azumarill.
  • Psychic Fangs is for Pecharunt and Iron Hands.
  • Bullet Punch targets Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales.
  • Earthquake hits Iron Crown, Hisuian Goodra, Registeel, and has favorable odds to beat most Raging Bolt sets.
  • The HP investment allows Metagross to survive Earthquake from Choice Band Iron Hands, while the Special Defense EVs allow it to survive Dark Pulse from Choice Specs Porygon-Z. The Attack EVs and an Adamant nature allow it to beat Encore + Disable Iron Valiant due to Struggle 2HKOing after a Bullet Punch.
  • An alternative EV spread of 232 HP / 236 Atk / 40 Def can be used to survive Focus Blast from Timid Choice Specs Iron Valiant and Earthquake from Choice Band Haxorus. The remaining EVs are put in Attack for maximum damage output.
  • Choice Band Metagross should almost always use the move that does the most damage to an opposing Pokemon. Notable exceptions to this rule are Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant, as Bullet Punch allows Metagross to beat Encore + Disable variants of these Pokemon.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• Choice Scarf Metagross trades winning matchups against foes like Choice Band Meowscarada and Encore + Disable Iron Valiant to have better matchups against both relatively faster Pokemon, like Garchomp and Iron Moth, and stall Pokemon, like Registeel and Cresselia.
  • Metagross should use Heavy Slam against Sylveon, Alolan Ninetales, Diancie, and Espathra.
  • Earthquake is especially strong on Metagross and is used to beat Iron Crown, Pecharunt, Iron Moth, and non-Liechi Berry Sneasler.
  • Trick allows Metagross deal with Registeel, Pecharunt, and Cresselia.
  • Ice Punch lets Metagross defeat Garchomp, Landorus, and non-Choice Scarf Landorus-T. Hammer Arm allows Metagross to defeat Porygon-Z and gives it the best matchup against Body Press Corviknight after using Trick.
  • The HP and Special Defense EVs allow Metagross to survive Tachyon Cutter from Weakness Policy Iron Crown four times, which lets Metagross use Trick before repeatedly using Earthquake to defeat it. It should be noted, however, that if Iron Crown's Booster Energy activates, Metagross should opt not to use Trick and use Earthquake repeatedly instead. The Speed EVs allow Metagross to outrun Iron Moth. The remaining EVs are in Attack to bolster its damage output.
  • Choice Scarf Metagross struggles against Water-types, such Manaphy, Volcanion, and some Primarina sets. It also struggles against certain Dragon-types, such as Choice Band Haxorus with Earthquake, Dragapult, and Raging Bolt. Choice Scarf Metagross, like other Metagross sets, also struggles against both Ursaluna formes and Dark-types like Hoopa-U, Zarude, and Chien-Pao. However, it also loses to Encore + Disable Iron Valiant, which no other Metagross set struggles with. To counteract these weaknesses, Fairy-type Pokemon like Sylveon can be good teammates, as they beats many of the Dark- and Dragon-types that Metagross struggles with. Choice Band Meowscarada is another good option, as it can beat many Water-types with Flower Trick while also beating many Dragon- and Grass-types that Metagross detests facing.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description: 180 Speed EVs let Metagross outspeed Adamant Tyranitar.
